ky_the_gallery.blurb: The Gallery is a sandstone wall in the Sore Heel Hollow part of the Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve, in the southern Red River Gorge. It is mostly a bolted sport crag with a handful of trad lines, and the grades sit in the middle of the range: the bulk of the climbs fall between 5.10 and 5.12, with a smaller group of 5.13s and only a few routes below 5.10. Expect the usual Red style of pockets, edges and sustained pulling on steep rock. The preserve is a popular destination, so weekends in spring and fall can be busy, and some of the roads in are rough, so allow extra time for the drive.

_expect.name: Graining Fork Nature Preserve (a.k.a. Roadside Crag)

ky_graining_fork_nature_preserve_a_k_a_r.blurb: Roadside Crag is a pocketed, south-facing sandstone wall beside KY 11 in the Natural Bridge region of the Red River Gorge. It is mainly a sport crag, with some trad lines and a couple of boulder problems, and the grades run wide: a good spread of moderates from 5.7 through 5.10 sits alongside a thick band of 5.12s, so it suits mixed groups. The wall faces the sun, which helps on cold days and makes midsummer afternoons uncomfortable. The walk from the road is short, which makes it an easy place to squeeze in a half day.
ky_graining_fork_nature_preserve_a_k_a_r.parking_note: Pull into the developed picnic-style parking area on the right side of KY 11 as you head into Wolfe County. The trail to the wall begins directly across the highway.
ky_graining_fork_nature_preserve_a_k_a_r.approach: Cross the highway from the parking area and follow the marked trail a short distance to the base of the wall.

ky_pistol_ridge.blurb: Pistol Ridge is a gray sandstone ridge in the Northern Gorge, off Indian Creek Road. It is a mixed bag: about half the climbs are trad, a good number are boulder problems mostly in the V0 to V2 range, and a few are sport routes. Most of the roped climbing is moderate, with the bulk of the routes between 5.6 and 5.10, and the cliff is tall but many lines are short. The rock can hold dampness for a while after rain and the quality is a bit uneven, so it rewards dry days. The hike in is long and starts steeply.
ky_pistol_ridge.parking_note: Pull off near the bridge where Indian Creek Road (FS 9) splits, then walk a few yards down the right fork to find the trail.

me_otter_cliffs.blurb: Otter Cliffs is a sea cliff of pink granite on Mount Desert Island in Acadia National Park, about 60 feet tall, with the Atlantic at its base. Top-roping is the norm here, anchored from the fixed bolts along the rim, and most of the routes fall between 5.6 and 5.10 with a few harder cracks and faces above that, so it is a favorite for newer climbers and guided groups. Check the tide table before you go, since high tide or heavy surf can swamp the ledge at the bottom and wet the ropes. Summer weekends are busy; spring and fall are calmer and cooler.

me_clifford_park.blurb: Clifford Park is a wooded city park in Biddeford with granite boulders and old quarry blocks scattered along a network of trails. Nearly all of the climbing is bouldering, with a few top-rope lines, and it leans easy to moderate: most problems are V0 to V3, with a small number of harder ones reaching into the double digits. Lichen is a factor on some rocks, and bugs are heavy in warm months, so early spring and late fall tend to be the pleasant windows. The park abuts private land, so stay on the trails and keep the place clean.
me_clifford_park.parking_note: Use the main lot by the playground off Pool Street in Biddeford.
me_clifford_park.approach: From the lot, head into the park and walk the Black Loop trail counter-clockwise toward the west side, where most of the problems are clustered.

me_04_barrett_s_cove_cliff.blurb: Barrett's Cove Cliff is a roughly 250-foot wall above Megunticook Lake and Route 52 in Camden Hills State Park, and it is the most convenient climbing in the Camden area. Most routes are traditional, usually two pitches, with face climbing on crimps, pockets and horizontal breaks and the occasional runout, so a rack with small gear is useful. Grades run from easy 5.3 to about 5.10, with the bulk in the 5.7 to 5.9 range. The right side tends to stay damp deep into summer. Descend by walking off to the left or making two rappels. In cold winters a few ice lines form.
me_04_barrett_s_cove_cliff.parking_note: Park along Route 52 a little south of the road down to the town beach on Megunticook Lake, using the paved pulloff.

md_hades_heights.blurb: Hades Heights is the taller and sunnier of the two main cliffs at Carderock, on the Potomac in the C&O Canal park. The climbing is on gray schist up to about 40 feet and is mostly top-rope, with a smaller number of trad lines and some boulder problems. Grades spread widely, from beginner-friendly 5.0s up through 5.12, with a lot of the weight around 5.9 to 5.11. Anchors are usually trees well back from the edge, so bring slings or a static line. The sun is welcome in cold months but makes summer days hot and humid, and the area can fill up at peak times.
md_hades_heights.parking_note: From the Clara Barton Parkway, use the northernmost Carderock lot. Keep valuables out of the car, since break-ins have happened there.
md_hades_heights.approach: Follow the trail west past the restroom building down to the base of the cliffs, a few hundred yards from the lot.

md_tiers_the.blurb: The Tiers is a bouldering area on Elk Ridge behind Maryland Heights, across the Potomac from Harpers Ferry. The rock is hard quartzite, the same stone that makes Maryland Heights itself such a good crack and edge cliff. Almost everything here is a boulder problem, with just a few trad and top-rope lines, and the grades are friendly: most problems are V0 to V3, with a few V4 and V5s for the stronger crowd. It sits on national park land, so stay on the trails.

_conflicts.me_04_barrett_s_cove_cliff: rock: stored schist, sources say granite (https://rockaroundtheworld.co.uk/2019/09/29/barretts-cove-cliff-camden-hills/); also aspect null stored, MP says faces southeast (https://www.mountainproject.com/area/106174857/barretts-cove-cliff)
